label: Clock in at the job site
text: The construction site wakes before the sun does: forklifts coughing, radios arguing, wet concrete breathing cold through Billy's boots. A yellow safety sign reads EVERYBODY GOES HOME TODAY. Somebody has written underneath it: PROBABLY. Billy's time card waits beside a frozen punch clock, and the foreman is already pointing him toward the beam crew.

choices.label: Read the safety board before joining the crew
choices.resultText: Billy slows down long enough to notice the beam tag is wrong by one digit. The mistake sticks in his head like a splinter.

choices.label: Clock in fast and get to the beam crew
choices.resultText: Billy stamps his card so hard the clock coughs. The crew cheers the speed. The site answers with a metal groan nobody quite admits hearing.

choices.label: Cover for a late coworker and take his first task
choices.resultText: Billy pockets a second task slip. It feels generous until the assignment routes him closer to the suspended beam.

label: Inspect the wrong-sounding beam
text: The beam hangs over the work lane with the patience of a held breath. Its chain ticks once, then again. The foreman barks for progress, the crew waits for Billy's signal, and the broken time clock clicks even though nobody is touching it.

choices.label: Call the hazard in and make everyone wait
choices.resultText: The foreman swears, but he waves two workers back. For one clean second Billy thinks procedure might save the day.

choices.label: Keep the lane moving and trust the rigging
choices.resultText: The site rewards confidence with momentum. It also rewards it with a louder tick from the chain.

choices.label: Step under the beam and fix the tag yourself
choices.resultText: Billy moves before anyone can stop him. The wrong tag peels loose in his hand, and underneath it is a number that looks almost like his name.

label: Billy's final moment
text: The chain gives up with a sound like a giant zipper. The beam falls. Time stretches thin enough for Billy to see every possible version of himself: the one who runs, the one who reaches, the one who laughs because the safety sign was technically a threat.

choices.label: Shove the nearest coworker out of the lane
choices.resultText: Billy hits the coworker hard enough to save him. The beam answers harder. The last thing Billy hears on Earth is someone screaming his name like it might still work.

choices.label: Grab the wrong beam tag before it vanishes
choices.resultText: Billy closes his fist around the tag. The world goes white, then black, then bureaucratic blue.

choices.label: Brace, look up, and refuse to look away
choices.resultText: Billy watches the impossible arrive. For a heartbeat, the beam stops watching him back. Then the job site is gone.

label: A numbered door hums in the Veilway
text: A brass plate reads 13,11. The door hums like it remembers you first.

choices.label: Inspect seams and run pattern check
Mark the frame and log it for Jinx

label: The numbered lock demands a response
text: The lock requests either a memory signature or a compliance stamp. Both routes are legal. Neither is clean.

choices.label: Use memory signature to open it sideways
Use intake stamp to force official access

label: A mirror chamber asks for testimony
text: Inside, three mirrored versions of your worst decision ask for your final statement.

choices.label: Own the memory without editing it
Rewrite the memory for strategic gain

label: Window 7B Intake: learn the floor rules
text: Window 7B opens with the sound of a tired throat clearing. The case worker behind it has typewriter keys for fingers and a cloud of blue carbon paper where a face should be. "Number?" they ask. Before Billy can answer, the ticket dispenser prints NEXT, SPECIAL PROCESSING, and OH NO on the same slip.

choices.label: Sign the intake slate and run the floor drill
choices.resultText: The case worker stamps APPROPRIATELY COOPERATIVE across Billy's shadow. The stamp is cold, official, and a little too pleased with itself.

choices.label: Push back on procedure and ask who wrote the rules
choices.resultText: The case worker finally looks up. Somewhere inside the carbon-paper cloud, a smile almost happens. "Unauthorized curiosity," they say, and slide Billy a form with one extra page.

choices.label: Watch the Afterlife Rolodex while they pretend it is not moving
choices.resultText: The Rolodex spins by itself: VEILWAY, ARCHIVE, BLACK MARKET, then a blank card with Billy's name typed sideways. The case worker slams it shut too late.

label: Intake Form: decode section headers
text: Window 7B slides over a tri-fold intake form thick enough to qualify as furniture. Its section headers keep reordering: CAUSE, ACCOUNTABILITY, CARRYOVER, and PLEASE DO NOT BLEED ON THE PAPERWORK. "Match intent before detail," the case worker says. "The scanner hates sincerity but respects consistency."

choices.label: Align each header to its matching memory thread
choices.resultText: Billy lets the form breathe before answering. The headers settle into a sequence that feels less like truth and more like something truth can survive inside.

choices.label: Force a fast pass and lock the headers early
choices.resultText: The form accepts the rushed order with a little cough of sparks. A nearby filing cabinet whispers, "Bold," in a voice that has rejected centuries of applications.

choices.label: Ask which section they removed before handing it over
choices.resultText: The case worker's typewriter fingers pause over the stamp pad. "You noticed the missing page. That's either a problem or an aptitude."

label: A lost ticket lies face-down near the chairs
text: A number card sits on the floor like it fell out of someone’s life on purpose. The ink is fresh. The paper is warm. The queue pretends not to see it.

choices.label: Return it to the counter and pretend you never touched it
choices.resultText: The case worker accepts it without looking up. The ticket disappears into a drawer labeled LIABILITY. A stamp lands somewhere out of sight. Something about the air feels marginally less hungry.

choices.label: Pocket the ticket (it is probably nothing)
choices.resultText: Billy palms it. The paper sticks for a second, like it wants to stay visible. When it finally slides free, the number on the top line has changed. The queue remains polite. The kind of polite that watches.

choices.label: Tear it in half and leave the pieces on the chair
choices.resultText: The paper does not tear cleanly. It resists like fabric. The halves still print a full number each. Across the room, a printer coughs and begins making duplicates of Billy’s name.

label: Breakroom vending machine: EXACT CHANGE FOR THE DEAD
text: The breakroom smells like burnt coffee and old rules. A vending machine offers EXACT CHANGE FOR THE DEAD. The coin slot is shaped like a small, patient mouth.

choices.label: Feed it Scrap (like it is a normal machine)
choices.resultText: The machine swallows the Scrap and dispenses a warm paper cup of something labeled COMFORT. It tastes like a memory you do not own. The office lights soften for exactly one blink.

choices.label: Offer it a small memory (just one)
choices.resultText: The machine hums like it is purring. The cup that drops tastes perfect. Billy cannot remember why. The machine prints a second receipt, longer than the first, listing new debts in tiny type.

choices.label: Back away. Let it keep its mouth.
choices.resultText: Billy steps away. The machine clicks once, disappointed. The office resumes its normal hum, which is somehow worse than before.

label: Intake Form: identity proof fields
text: Three lines request proof of who Billy was, who Billy is, and who profits if those answers do not match. The paper warms under their hand. Behind the glass, the case worker says, "Do not worry. The form already has opinions."

choices.label: File a direct record with no edits
choices.resultText: Billy writes the plain answer. The office lights flicker, not because the answer is wrong, but because unedited truth makes this place work harder.

choices.label: Edit one line to conceal your leverage
choices.resultText: Billy changes one line. The ink dries instantly, like it had been waiting to become useful instead of honest.

choices.label: Write: identity cannot be reduced to three boxes
choices.resultText: The form tries to reject the sentence. Then the sentence rejects the form. The case worker marks the margin: philosophically inconvenient.

label: Intake Form: witness signature required
text: A red bar flashes: WITNESS REQUIRED. The case worker keeps stamping other souls while Billy's line blinks unanswered. Every stamp sounds like a door choosing not to open.

choices.label: Request official witness signature from the case worker
choices.resultText: The case worker signs with a pen made of compressed policy. "I did not see anything," they say, which apparently counts as witnessing in three departments.

choices.label: Forge the witness line with an archive stamp
choices.resultText: The archive stamp lands perfectly. Too perfectly. Somewhere deep in the office, a drawer opens to create a file labeled FUTURE PROBLEM.

choices.label: Ask why Billy's file needs a witness at all
choices.resultText: "Repeat anomalies require corroboration," the case worker says, then realizes they said repeat. The stamp hovers in midair, embarrassed.

label: Window 7B review: submit intake form
text: The case worker feeds Billy's packet into the Soul Scanner. The machine chews, thinks, and prints a route profile with several lines blacked out before the ink is dry. "Approved forms unlock orientation," the case worker says. "Rejected forms loop. Missing forms become management."

choices.label: Submit clean and accept your profile
choices.resultText: The scanner prints CLEAN ENOUGH FOR GOVERNMENT WORK. The case worker files it quickly, before the machine can reconsider.

choices.label: Submit with risk markers and keep your options open
choices.resultText: The scanner prints RISKY BUT INTERESTING. The case worker folds the report in half, hiding a second destination line from the overhead camera.

choices.label: Keep a carbon copy before the scanner eats the packet
choices.resultText: Billy palms the carbon copy. The case worker sees it happen and chooses to adjust a paperclip instead of sounding the alarm.

label: Stat Generator orientation and Rolodex briefing
text: The case worker leads Billy to the Stat Generator, a brass-and-neon machine built like a slot machine that got tenure. The Afterlife Rolodex spins beside it, flashing hidden pathways faster than the worker can cover them. "Ignore those," they say. "Those are not for first-time deaths."

choices.label: Choose Veilway track from Rolodex index
choices.resultText: Billy pulls toward the Veilway card. The Stat Generator coughs out a clean route, then quietly prints a second card upside down.

choices.label: Choose Executor track from Rolodex index
choices.resultText: Billy watches the Executor track light up. The case worker's fingers hover over the cancel stamp, but the machine has already tasted the choice.

choices.label: Let the glitch mark touch the Stat Generator
choices.resultText: The lever shocks Billy's palm. Stats spill out as nonsense, then as prophecy, then as a lunch menu for someone named Murray. The case worker whispers, "Special processing," like a curse.

label: Clearance release: first gate assignment
text: The release counter looks like a service window and a judge's bench had a child nobody wants to claim. Window 7B slides Billy a packet warm from the machine. The top page says CLEARED FOR LIVE ROUTES. The carbon copy says IF HE ASKS WHO CLEARED HIM, DO NOT ANSWER. The clerk taps the stamp pad and says, "Choose how official you want this to look."

choices.label: Accept the official packet and deploy clean
choices.resultText: Billy accepts the packet without flinching. The stamp lands clean, the gate lights green, and the office files him under COOPERATIVE BUT UNUSUAL.
choices.resultEvent: Callback armed: official release posture recorded.

choices.label: Pocket the carbon copy before leaving
choices.resultText: Billy palms the forbidden carbon copy while the clerk pretends not to see. The gate opens, but a side printer begins quietly making duplicates of his name.
choices.resultEvent: Callback armed: stolen release copy can surface later.

choices.label: Ask who approved the clearance
choices.resultText: The case worker's smile freezes for exactly one second. A name is blacked out while Billy watches. The gate opens anyway, and now he knows someone upstream is protecting the file from both sides.
choices.resultEvent: Callback armed: clearance sponsor questioned.

label: Jinx cuts through the queue with a broken compass
text: Jinx slides out from behind a vending machine labeled EXACT CHANGE FOR THE DEAD. His compass is cracked, ticking backward, and pointing directly at Billy's chest. "I can get you through unseen," he whispers. "Or I can tell you why unseen things keep finding you. Pick fast. The line is pretending not to move."

choices.label: Trust Jinx and follow the side route now
choices.resultText: Jinx grins like he just stole a door. The side route folds open, skipping the worst patrol angles, but it also marks Billy as someone willing to leave the official line.
choices.resultEvent: Callback armed: Jinx follow posture recorded.

choices.label: Stop him and demand the catch first
choices.resultText: Jinx hates the delay, but respect flickers under the panic. He gives Billy a gate-code fragment and refuses to say whose pocket it came from.
choices.resultEvent: Callback armed: Jinx interrogation posture recorded.

choices.label: Take his compass reading but choose your own route
choices.resultText: Billy studies the compass without taking Jinx's hand. The needle jerks from heartbeat to exit sign to something underneath the floor. Jinx laughs once, nervous and impressed. "Okay. You might be trouble."
choices.resultEvent: Callback armed: Jinx independent-route posture recorded.

label: Edgar the Raven opens a ledger with Billy already itemized
text: A raven lands on the filing cart and the cart immediately applies for hazard pay. Edgar opens a black ledger to Billy's name. Under BALANCE DUE, someone has written NOT MONEY in careful red ink. "Everyone pays," Edgar croaks. "Question is whether you pay now, later, or cleverly enough to make me curious."

choices.label: Pay now with a Scripted Note and ask for one true lead
choices.resultText: Edgar takes the note, weighs it like a small bone, and drops a true rumor into Billy's palm. "Prompt payment," he says. "Rare. Suspicious. Useful."
choices.resultEvent: Callback armed: Edgar early-payment ledger opened.

choices.label: Refuse the bargain and watch the ledger instead
choices.resultText: Billy keeps his payment. Edgar respects the refusal just enough to become annoying about it. The ledger twitches, revealing a pattern in who gets billed before they remember why.
choices.resultEvent: Callback armed: Edgar refusal invoice opened.

choices.label: Ask Edgar to prove the debt chain
choices.resultText: Edgar goes very still. Then he turns the ledger around. Three signatures are missing, one is Billy's in handwriting he has never used, and one belongs to an office that should not exist.
choices.resultEvent: Callback armed: Edgar chain-of-custody challenge opened.

label: Nyx applies pressure without making a sound
text: The lights narrow to a corridor made of breath. Nyx circles Billy in absolute silence, shadow paws touching places the floor has not admitted exist. It waits for fear, discipline, or the first honest boundary. Somewhere in the dark, a chain drags once and stops.

choices.resultText: Billy does not run. Nyx accepts the challenge by backing away one exact step, which somehow feels less like mercy than measurement.
choices.resultEvent: Callback armed: Nyx open-stance pressure recorded.

choices.label: Retreat and break line of sight
choices.resultText: Billy breaks the line cleanly. Nyx lets him go, but the silence follows with a new rhythm, already learning the shape of his exits.
choices.resultEvent: Callback armed: Nyx retreat pattern recorded.

choices.resultText: Billy says where the hunt stops. Nyx tilts its head, not offended, not obedient. The boundary glows for one breath before the floor swallows it as evidence.

text: The Processing Agent opens Billy's anomaly file with silver gloves and no expression. REALITY_MANIPULATION: HIGH blinks at the top. "This is not a confession," the agent says. "It is calibration. Truth, omission, and accusation all fit different machines."

choices.resultText: The true record accepts Billy's signature and burns a small honest circle into the page. The case worker relaxes, which somehow makes the room feel more dangerous.
choices.resultEvent: Callback armed: honest anomaly disclosure logged.

choices.resultEvent: Callback armed: partial anomaly disclosure logged.

choices.label: Demand to see who flagged the anomaly

choices.resultEvent: Callback armed: anomaly source challenge logged.

label: Soul Resonance Pattern
text: The Soul Resonance scanner unfolds from the counter like an old church organ made of receipt paper. Three harmonic lanes spin through the glass: remembered heartbeat, loudest fear, and a quiet illegal signal that only appears when nobody admits it is there. The machine accepts any lock, but the residue follows Billy.

choices.resultText: Billy follows the heartbeat instead of the machine's impatience. The scanner prints a clean resonance mark and, for one blessed second, the room says his name correctly.
choices.resultEvent: Callback armed: true resonance posture recorded.

choices.label: Force the strongest lane into compliance
choices.resultText: Billy grabs the loudest lane and makes it obey. Clearance prints in red, nearby clerks pretend not to hear the alarm, and the scanner remembers the shape of his pressure.
choices.resultEvent: Callback armed: forced resonance posture recorded.

choices.resultEvent: Callback armed: hidden resonance lane heard.

choices.resultEvent: Teaching beat: misread resonance still clears the desk.

label: Life Recognition Trial

choices.resultEvent: Callback armed: full memory witnessed.

choices.label: Accept the official summary without witnessing
choices.resultText: Billy takes the redacted summary to move the line. It works — and the missing witness presses harder against the glass afterward.
choices.resultEvent: Teaching beat: rushed recognition clears the desk with a cost.

choices.label: Redact the memory for utility

choices.resultEvent: Callback armed: official redaction chosen.

choices.label: Name the missing witness instead of the memory

choices.resultEvent: Callback armed: missing witness named.
